llm.summary: The skill's commands match its combat purpose, but the instructions assume access to local signing keys, a structsd CLI, auto-submitted transactions, and long-running CPU work while the registry metadata claims no credentials or binaries—this mismatch and the auto-submit behavior are concerning.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (combat/raids/stealth) aligns with the CLI commands in SKILL.md: scouting, stealth activation, attacks, fleet-move, raid PoW compute, etc. However the metadata declares no required binaries or credentials while the instructions clearly require the structsd CLI and access to signing keys (the repeated --from [key-name] flags). That mismatch is noteworthy.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to run transaction commands that sign and submit on-chain operations (frequently using -y to auto-accept), and to run long-running PoW compute in background terminals. These steps can irreversibly move assets or consume significant CPU. The SKILL.md also relies on local key names and implicit local keystore access without stating where keys live or requiring confirmation—granting an agent ability to execute these steps could cause unwanted, irreversible actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files, so nothing new is written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential, yet runtime instructions repeatedly require signing keys (--from [key-name]) and assume the structsd CLI is present and configured. The skill therefore implicitly requires access to local credentials and a networked node or RPC endpoint. It also instructs resource-intensive PoW compute, which can abuse CPU resources. The undeclared need for credentials and binaries is disproportionate and unclear.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent installation or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (not set to disabled) — this is normal but combined with the auto-submit instructions increases risk.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a coherent combat/raid operator for a game-like system, but it assumes you have the structsd CLI and local signing keys and will run commands that auto-confirm and submit transactions. Before installing or allowing the agent to use this skill: 1) Do not give it access to real account keys—test with a throwaway account. 2) Verify the structsd binary and keystore locations; the skill metadata should be updated to declare those requirements. 3) Remove or require manual confirmation for flags like -y/auto-submit so actions are not executed without human consent. 4) Be aware planet-raid-compute is CPU-intensive—run only on machines you control and accept the load. 5) Consider the ethical/legal implications of automated attack/raid operations in your environment. If the publisher cannot explain why credentials/binaries are omitted from the metadata, treat the skill cautiously or avoid installing it.
